newsitem.title: INDIA: India BSE chief sees top shr index at 5,000 in Oct.
newsitem.headline: India BSE chief sees top shr index at 5,000 in Oct.

text.p: The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) president Madan Gopal Damani said on Monday he expected the BSE's benchmark 30-share index to touch 5,000 by October.
"If the moonson is good, by Diwali, I expect the index to reach 5,000," Damani told reporters at a press conference in Bombay.
Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights falls in late October.
"This is being conservative," the BSE chief said. "It will be a slow, steady rise."
On Monday, the BSE 30-share index closed at a provisional 3,870.34.
It had earlier touched an eight-month high of 4007.91.
Damani said the rise was a fall-out of the broking community's enthusiasm for the 1997/98 (April-March) budget, unveiled last week.

"Except cynics I don't think there's anyone who is not happy with the budget," Damani said. "The only occasion in the last 50 years when there was such jubilation was over the 1985 budget of V.P. Singh."
Singh, who later became prime minister, was then finance minister in the government of former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi.
Damani told Reuters he expected the index to rise to about the 4,500-level over the next three or four months.
"I think it will get halfway there during the next three or four months, that is about 4,500," Damani said. "It will be steady growth."
